hook: Most reviews go quiet after the first few hundred buyers.

scenes.voiceover: 349,254 reviews is more than most gyms have members.

scenes.visual_prompt: Slow push-in on the scale's display, numbers crisp and lit, shallow depth of field, neutral bathroom background
scenes.voiceover: That's not marketing. That's how many people came back to rate a bathroom scale.

scenes.visual_prompt: Split composition: a dusty forgotten gadget in a drawer on one side, the clean scale in use on the other, contrasty side light
scenes.voiceover: Cheap electronics usually go quiet after the first thousand buyers. This one didn't.

scenes.visual_prompt: Bare feet stepping onto the scale, low angle, bathroom floor, natural daylight, calm unhurried motion
scenes.voiceover: The Etekcity Digital Body Weight Bathroom Scale does one thing — you step on, you get your weight. Holding 4.7 stars across that many reviews is a durability signal from people using it daily.

scenes.visual_prompt: Scale tucked neatly against a bathroom wall beside a folded towel, warm lamp light, tidy and lived-in
scenes.voiceover: A scale the crowd already stress-tested for you. Sixteen dollars and eighty-seven cents.

caption:
Most reviews go quiet after the first few hundred buyers.

Cheap gear usually stops getting rated once the early rush of buyers has said their piece. When a listing keeps collecting reviews long after launch, that's the crowd still bothering to weigh in.

This pick is still pulling in ratings well past its first wave of buyers — people rating it after actually living with it, not just unboxing it.

That kind of staying power tells you more than any spec sheet, whatever the price tag says today.
